sn44.2:2.5: “Here, sir, I stay not far from the Buddha in a wilderness hut.
sn44.2:2.6: Then, sir, several wanderers of other religions went up to me and exchanged greetings with me.
sn44.2:2.7: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, sir, those wanderers of other religions said this to me:
sn44.2:2.8: ‘Reverend Anurādha, when a realized one is describing a realized one—a supreme person, highest of people, who has reached the highest point—they describe them in these four ways:
sn44.2:2.9: “After death, a realized one still exists” or …
sn44.2:2.10: “After death, a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists”’?
sn44.2:2.11: When I had said this, sir, those wanderers of other religions said this to me:
sn44.2:2.12: ‘Reverends, when a realized one is describing a realized one—a supreme person, highest of people, who has reached the highest point—they describe them other than these four ways:
sn44.2:2.13: “After death, a realized one still exists” or …
sn44.2:2.14: “After death, a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists”?’
sn44.2:2.15: When they had said this, sir, those wanderers of other religions said this to me:
sn44.2:2.16: ‘This mendicant must be junior, recently gone forth, or else a foolish, incompetent senior mendicant.’
sn44.2:2.17: Then, sir, after rebuking me by calling me “junior” and “foolish”, those wanderers of other religions rose from their seats and left.
sn44.2:2.18: Soon after they had left, sir, this occurred to me among those wanderers of other religions:
sn44.2:2.19: ‘If those wanderers were to inquire further, how should I answer them so as to repeat what the Buddha has said, and not misrepresent him with an untruth? How should I explain in line with his teaching, so that there would be no legitimate grounds for rebuttal and criticism’?”
sn44.2:17.10: ‘After death, a realized one neither still exists nor no longer exists’?
